chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Maymun al-Bann, who said:
I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),
verses from the chapter of Hud were recited in his presence.
So when it reached the verse: 'And We rained upon them stones of clay, one after another, marked with your Lord, and it is not far from the unjust.'
He said: 'The one who dies persisting upon sodomy will not die until Allah pelt him with a stone from those stones, in which his death will occur, and no one will see it.'

key_terms.هُود: The Prophet Hud (peace be upon him) / Chapter of Hud

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'stones of clay' in Surah Hud according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the 'stones of clay' (hijarat min sijjil) in Surah Hud as a specific divine punishment for those who persist in sodomy (al-lawat), linking the Quranic narrative of Lot's people to a tangible sign of death. He specifies that the individual will be struck by a marked stone from this collection, which causes their demise in a manner unseen by others, emphasizing the precision of divine retribution. This hadith is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the severity of the sin and the certainty of its punishment in this life or the hereafter.
